analysis.title: 2027 US Economics Outlook: Resilient Growth, Reluctant Disinflation
key_insights: Base case is resilient growth with reluctant disinflation. Real GDP grows 2.5% in 2027 and 2.7% in 2028 (4Q/4Q, per the forecast tables). Growth is driven by AI-related capex and wealth-supported upper-income consumer spending, without overheating the labor market.

Hyperscaler capex is forecast at $1.6tn in 2027 and $1.8tn in 2028, up from $951bn in 2026. Growth slows from 98% in 2026 to 73% in 2027 and 7% in 2028. AI-related spending contributes 0.9pp to GDP growth in 2027, and the contribution is expected to peak in 2027.

Much of AI capex leaks into imports. 60-70% of hyperscaler capex goes to computers and peripherals, nearly all imported. Net trade is a drag of about 0.6pp on GDP in 2027 and 2028, versus -1.1pp in 2026. Real imports are forecast to grow 5.1% and 5.7% against exports of 2.1% and 3.1%.

Non-AI business investment slows in 2027 because of Fed hikes and higher energy prices, then recovers in 2028. Nonresidential fixed investment growth is 9.3% in 2026, 6.9% in 2027 and 8.4% in 2028. From 2028 the AI spending mix shifts from infrastructure to adoption (software).

Real consumption growth slows from 2.4% in 2026 to 2.0% in 2027 and rebounds to 2.3% in 2028. Low- and middle-income consumers lead the slowdown, and goods spending slows more than services. Household net wealth is up about $20.6tn in four quarters, and about 75% of net worth sits with upper-income households. Wealth effects added about 0.6pp to real consumption growth over the four quarters ending 3Q26. The saving rate fell from 5.0% to 3.8%.

The Democratic midterm sweep creates upside risk to consumption. A delay of OBBBA Medicaid/SNAP cuts could add 10bp (targeted delay) to 40bp (full delay) to 2027 consumption growth. Earliest passage is 1Q27, more likely mid-2027, possibly tied to debt-ceiling talks.

Fiscal policy turns roughly neutral for 2027 growth after a roughly 40bp boost in 2026. The deficit is $2.03tn (6.2% of GDP) in 2026 and $2.02tn (5.9%) in 2027, and 6.1% in 2028. Debt hits the statutory limit in February 2027, with a projected x-date in late 3Q27 after $300-350bn of extraordinary measures.

Core PCE is forecast to slow from 3.2% in 2026 to 2.6% in 2027 and 2.2% in 2028 (4Q/4Q). Headline PCE slows from 3.8% to 2.3% to 2.1%. Disinflation drivers: tariff payback (-30bp), airfares (-20bp), smaller AI boost to goods (-10bp) and rents (-5bp). Offsets: broader energy pass-through (+15bp) and healthcare (+5bp). Clear disinflation may not show until 2Q27 because of first-quarter price resets.

The Fed is expected to hike 25bp in December and again in March to 4.25-4.50%. It then holds through 2027 and cuts 75bp in 2028 to 3.50-3.75%. Risks to the near-term path skew toward higher rates if inflation sticks or the labor market tightens.

The labor market stays low-hire/low-fire. Payroll growth is forecast at 70k a month in 2026 and 35k in 2027 and 2028, against an estimated breakeven of about 50k. Unemployment drifts from 4.2% in 4Q26 to 4.3% at end-2027 and 4.4% at end-2028. AI displacement adds at most 15bp to unemployment, concentrated among young workers in exposed occupations.

Morgan Stanley's real neutral rate estimate has risen to about 150bp, between 100bp (HLW) and 185bp (Lubik-Matthes), implying a nominal neutral of about 3.5%. The estimate has wide confidence bands and may be biased upward by supply shocks.

Fed Chair Warsh is expected to push balance sheet reform. The base case is about $1.5tn of reduction over roughly two years (range $0.6-2.5tn) starting as early as 1Q27 or 2Q27, within an ample-reserves regime. Tools are tiered interest on reserves (50-75bp lower above a threshold), discount-window collateral recognition for liquidity rules, a smaller TGA, and bill-heavy Treasury funding. The report expects less Fed communication, with major changes needing a committee vote.

Active MBS sales are the main balance-sheet risk. MS assigns a 15% probability to sales of up to $5bn a month. Reducing MBS by $20bn a month could widen lower-coupon spreads about 10bp, and $35bn a month about 20bp. A deliberate move to scarce reserves would raise repo and funding volatility.

Housing stays weak. The Fed hikes keep the 10-year Treasury near 5.0% at end-2027, falling to 4.75% at end-2028, and mortgage rates stay at or above 7% through 2027 (6.75% by end-2028). Real residential investment is flat in 2027 and up 1.5% in 2028. Homebuilder confidence was at its lowest since 2012 in October.

Trend productivity growth has risen from about 1.6% in 2019 to 2.1% as of 3Q26, and is forecast at 2.3%. The gains come mainly from capital deepening in high-AI-exposure industries rather than broad adoption. Potential GDP growth is about 2.2% because trend hours slowed to 0.3%.

Scenario probabilities are baseline 45%, aggregate demand upside 20%, AI slowdown 15%, productivity upside 10% and oil/rates downside 10%. The demand upside has GDP at 3.4% in 2027 and the Fed hiking to 5.625%. The AI slowdown has GDP at 0.2%, unemployment at 5.0% and the Fed cutting to 1.375%. The oil/rates downside has oil at $125-150, GDP at 0.5% and the Fed at 5.375%.

The report sees more supply chain rewiring than reshoring. Import penetration of all goods rose from about 25% in 2005 to about 33% in 2024. Machinery is the clearest case of substitution, but the gains are concentrated in AI-related categories. Brent is assumed to stay near current levels, with a higher oil risk premium from the Middle East conflict.

sector_views.rationale: Hyperscaler capex is forecast at $1.6tn in 2027 and $1.8tn in 2028. Hyperscalers are highly rated issuers projecting returns well above their cost of capital, though 2028 growth slows to 7%.
Mortgage rates at or above 7% and the lock-in effect keep real residential investment flat in 2027 and up 1.5% in 2028.
Goods spending slows more than services in 2027 because of tighter financial conditions and fading fiscal support. Real goods consumption growth is 1.4% in 2027, against 2.3% in 2026.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Resilient, investment-led growth. 3Q26E is 3.4% and 4Q26E is 2.2% annualized.
Sticky disinflation. Core stays above the 2% target through 2028 because of energy pass-through and AI demand.
Headline falls faster than core as energy payback and tariff effects fade.
Energy payback drives the 2027 drop. Core CPI is 2.8%, 2.4% and 2.3%.
Two 25bp hikes, a hold through 2027, then 75bp of cuts in 2028. The year-end 2026 midpoint is 4.125%.
A slow drift higher from weak payroll growth of 35k a month, below the 50k breakeven.
Low-hire/low-fire equilibrium. Payrolls run slightly below the estimated 50k breakeven.
Implies a nominal neutral of 3.5% at 2% inflation. The current 3.75-4.0% range is neutral to moderately restrictive.
Deficits near 6% of GDP are the new norm. Debt/GDP stays near 125%.
Wage growth is decelerating from 3.9% a year earlier. ECI private compensation was 3.3% y/y in 3Q26.
Down from 5.0% at end-2025. There is limited room for further decline, so spending may weaken with a lag.
MS rates strategists' forecast. It keeps mortgage rates at or above 7% through 2027.
Up from a trough of 0.84% in March 2026.

risk_factors: AI investment shortfall. Weaker expected profitability, an equity repricing, or hyperscaler financing sensitivity to rates could cut capex, hit wealth effects and push unemployment to 5.1% in the AI slowdown scenario.
Political risk on data centers after the midterms, including permitting requirements, tighter regulation, and national security policies that delay buildouts.
Power, grid, construction and skilled labor bottlenecks that could stop compute capacity from coming online.
Upside inflation risk from energy pass-through into goods, a stronger consumer, a tight labor market, or renewed Middle East conflict.
Fed policy risk. An overheating labor market would bring more aggressive hikes, and a tilt toward scarce reserves or active MBS sales would cause funding volatility and wider mortgage spreads.
Fiscal and debt ceiling risk. The debt limit binds in February 2027 with a late 3Q27 x-date. Social Security trust fund exhaustion is projected in late 2032.
Oil shock to $125-150/bbl combined with Fed tightening in the stagflation scenario.
A weaker low- and middle-income consumer as the saving rate falls, real income growth is soft, and Medicaid/SNAP cuts bite.
charts_described: Exhibit 5 shows hyperscaler capex estimates of $155bn in 2022, $157bn in 2023, $262bn in 2024, $481bn in 2025, $951bn in 2026, $1,641bn in 2027 and $1,760bn in 2028.
Exhibit 6 shows annual hyperscaler capex growth of 67% in 2024, 84% in 2025, 98% in 2026, 73% in 2027 and 7% in 2028.
Exhibit 12 shows the top income quintile holds 72.6% of net worth as of 2Q26.
Exhibit 23 shows the deficit bridge from $2,034bn in 2026 to $2,016bn in 2027: OBBBA -118, tariffs -193, defense +144, interest +143, Social Security COLA +119 and other macro -112.
Exhibit 47 shows the MS real neutral rate rising from a bit below 100bp in 1Q25 to about 150bp in 2Q26.
Exhibit 49 shows policy options to reduce reserve demand: smaller TGA $170-340bn, reverse repo $0-300bn, tiered IORB $250-2,500bn and LCR/ILST reform $200-1,000bn, totaling $620bn-2.5tn.
vol_and_positioning: The report says AI-related fears have so far caused only a modest equity pullback and some spread widening.
A balance sheet runoff watch list: repo rates relative to IORB, the effective fed funds rate, swap spreads and dealer balance-sheet costs would give early signs of reserve scarcity.
Equity analysts expect double-digit percentage equity gains in 2027, which supports upper-income wealth effects.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict and the Iran war. The failed US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding in early July 2026 kept oil elevated. The baseline assumes a largely status quo conflict and Brent near current levels through 2027.
The oil shock scenario has Brent at $125-150/bbl if attempts to resolve the conflict fail. It has the Fed hiking to 5.375% and a mild recession in late 2027.
Defense spending tied to the Iran war supports 2.8% real government spending growth in 2026 and 3.0% in 2027.

Tariffs remain a feature. The effective tariff rate is expected to stay near 10%, and IEEPA-related refunds distorted 2026 customs receipts. Evidence of reshoring is thin, with trade being rerouted rather than production brought home.
The Democratic midterm sweep raises political risk for AI data center buildout. New governors could impose requirements that delay about 5GW of 2028 capacity in Texas and Ohio to 2029.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers are highly rated with projected returns far above their cost of capital. Equity analysts keep revising capex up, to $1.6tn in 2027 and $1.8tn in 2028, and AI supports upper-income wealth effects and productivity growth of 2.3%.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors fear that debt- and equity-financed AI investment may not generate cash flows quickly enough to justify valuations. In the AI slowdown scenario capex falls in 2027, asset prices drop, GDP grows 0.2% and unemployment reaches 5.0-5.1%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A decline in the level of AI capex in 2027, or investors cutting AI profitability expectations and triggering an equity market repricing.

tension_points.bull_case: A measured recalibration of two 25bp hikes to 4.25-4.50% is enough to restrain second-round energy effects without hurting AI investment. Warsh sees supply-driven productivity growth and a Fed that is not aiming to throw sand in the gears.
tension_points.bear_case: If AI spending spills into jobs and the labor market overheats, the Fed hikes at every meeting in 2027 to 5.625% (demand upside, 20% probability). The Fed could also hike further if oil spikes (5.375% in the oil downside).
tension_points.what_invalidates: Unemployment falling toward 3.5% with firming wages, or inflation showing no deceleration, would push the Fed toward a more aggressive path.

tension_points.bull_case: Wealth gains of $20.6tn support upper-income spending, and real wages turn positive in early 2027. A delay of OBBBA Medicaid/SNAP cuts could add up to 0.4pp to 2027 consumption growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Low- and middle-income consumers face a falling saving rate, soft real income, entitlement cuts and tighter policy. Large and persistent asset price declines would dent top-quintile spending.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A larger, more persistent equity market decline, which would cut upper-income spending, or a full delay of the SNAP/Medicaid cuts, which would lift 2027 consumption by up to 0.4pp.

tension_points.bull_case: Roughly $1.5tn of shrinkage via passive runoff, tiered IORB and bill-heavy Treasury funding keeps reserves ample and only modestly tightens financial conditions.
tension_points.bear_case: Coupon-heavy Treasury funding, active MBS sales (15% probability), or a return to scarce reserves could raise term premiums, widen MBS spreads by 10-20bp and add repo volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Treasury shifting to coupon-heavy issuance, MBS sales starting, or repo and funding spreads rising against IORB.

theme_stances.key_argument: AI-related spending stays on track despite tighter policy and monetization concerns, because most hyperscaler spending comes from highly rated issuers with returns far above their cost of capital.
theme_stances.evidence: the AI thesis remains intact, but we also acknowledge political risks have risen

theme_stances.key_argument: Slow disinflation and a labor market without overheating argue for a measured recalibration rather than an aggressive tightening cycle.
theme_stances.evidence: we expect two additional rate hikes from the Fed with 25bp increases

theme_stances.key_argument: The Fed can shrink its balance sheet by about $1.5tn while keeping ample reserves, with bill-heavy Treasury funding limiting the market impact.
